$Comment: Stone Talus rig. Offsets are model units (one prefab block) in titan-local space: +X right, +Y up, -Z forward. The root entity sits on the ground, so Pelvis's offset is the hip height.

Bone names and parenting mirror the vanilla player rig (Common/Characters/Player.blockymodel), minus everything a talus does not have: no head, neck, face, hair or clothing. Any character .blockyanim can then be pointed at a talus and will drive the bones it recognises. Belly, Chest and the two shoulders carry no prefab and no offset; they exist so that a borrowed animation rotating a player's spine or shoulder moves the parts hanging off them here too.

WeakpointSockets is a candidate list rather than a fixed set: each titan rolls WeakpointCountMin..Max of them at random. The body slab reaches 4.5 out in X and 2.0 in Y and Z, and every socket sits on that surface. The spawner centres a node on its socket and sinks it by the variant's WeakpointEmbed, so authoring one short of the surface would bury it completely.

Bones.$Comment: Origin is skipped. The player rig has one above Pelvis, but character clips use it to hold a fixed quarter-turn that would leave a talus dancing side-on to its target.
Bones.Name: Pelvis

Bones.$Comment: Spine joints, zero-length. A talus torso is one slab with no anatomy to space out, but the names have to be present or a borrowed clip's chest sway stops at the hips.
Bones.Name: Belly

Bones.$Comment: The body slab is authored 4 deep x 4 tall x 9 long, so it is yawed 90 degrees to put its long axis across the shoulders. Pivot is the centre of the slab. Hung off Chest rather than Pelvis so it leans with the spine, and the ore sockets sit on the same bone so they travel with it.
Bones.Name: Chest_Mesh

Bones.$Comment: Shoulders are zero-length pivots, as on the player rig, where the arm hangs off the shoulder at no offset. Arm segments are a 2x4x2 prefab. A bone's Scale sets both its thickness and its length, so the segment is authored long and narrow: at 0.85 it is 1.7 blocks thick and spans the 3.4 to the next joint. Shoulder (6.3) to wrist is 6.8, enough for the smash to plant a fist on the ground with the elbow still bent. The arms are the route up onto the back, so they run ColliderAllFaces with no thinning: an arm held out at an angle has no upward-facing voxels in its own prefab space, and thinning any segment leaves a gap the player cannot cross.
Bones.Name: L-Shoulder

Bones.$Comment: Pivot is the middle of the fist rather than the wrist, because the smash drives this bone's pivot to the impact point and a fist centred there reads as embedded in the ground. MirrorX reflects the shared hand prefab so the pair are opposite hands rather than two right ones.
Bones.Name: L-Hand

Bones.$Comment: Legs hang off Pelvis, as on the player rig. They carry no colliders: they swing fastest and a player anchored to one would be flung around. It also leaves the gap between them open, so a player can run under the body to escape a smash and come up behind.
Bones.Name: L-Thigh

IkChains.$Comment: RestOffset is measured from the Pelvis bone, which sits HipHeight above the ground, so Y is the drop back down to the feet.
IkChains.Name: Leg_L

IkChains.$Comment: The chain starts at the arm rather than the shoulder: the shoulder is a fixed pivot and a zero-length first bone would make the solver divide by zero.
IkChains.Name: Arm_L
